deck.name: Oceans & Water Bodies
deck.description: Ocean basins, tides, currents, rivers, lakes and the movement of water.

questions.prompt: Which ocean basin has the greatest surface area?
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers more area than all of Earth's land put together.

questions.prompt: Which ocean basin has the smallest surface area?
questions.explanation: The Arctic is also the shallowest ocean, and sea ice covers much of it.

questions.prompt: Which ocean surrounds Antarctica?
questions.explanation: National Geographic recognized the Southern Ocean as the fifth ocean in 2021.

questions.prompt: How many named ocean basins are commonly recognized?
questions.explanation: They are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic, all connected.

questions.prompt: What is the approximate average salinity of seawater?
questions.explanation: That is roughly 3.5% dissolved salts, not 35%.

questions.prompt: About what percentage of Earth's surface is covered by the ocean?
questions.explanation: The ocean also holds about 97% of Earth's water.

questions.prompt: Which celestial body has the stronger tide-generating effect on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun also affects tides, but the Moon is much closer to Earth.

questions.prompt: When do spring tides usually occur?
questions.explanation: Spring tides have nothing to do with the season. At new and full moon, the Sun and Moon line up and their pulls add together.

questions.prompt: When do neap tides usually occur?
questions.explanation: At the quarter moons, the Sun and Moon pull at right angles, so the tidal range is smallest.

questions.prompt: What produces most ordinary surface waves at sea?
questions.explanation: Wave size depends on wind speed, how long the wind blows, and the fetch, the stretch of open water it blows across.

questions.prompt: Which event can generate a tsunami by abruptly displacing seawater?
questions.explanation: A tsunami can cross an ocean about as fast as a jet plane and grows taller as it reaches shallow water.

questions.prompt: What is the continental shelf?
choices: A deep trench beside an island arc
A ridge formed above a mantle plume
A steep slope beneath an ocean ridge
questions.explanation: Shelves are usually less than about 200 m deep and hold many of the world's richest fishing grounds.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the deepest known point in the ocean?
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep, in the Mariana Trench, is about 10,900 m (35,800 ft) deep.

questions.prompt: In which ocean is the Mariana Trench?
questions.explanation: Its Challenger Deep, nearly 11,000 m down, is the deepest known point in the ocean.

questions.prompt: In which ocean does the Gulf Stream flow?
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico up the U.S. East Coast and across the Atlantic.

questions.prompt: Which pair of factors strongly influences seawater density and thermohaline circulation?
questions.explanation: Cold, salty water is denser and sinks, which helps drive the deep currents known as the global conveyor belt.

questions.prompt: Where does freshwater from land commonly mix with seawater?
questions.explanation: Chesapeake Bay is the largest estuary in the United States.

questions.prompt: What does brackish water contain?
choices: A mixture of fresh and salt water
A layer of freshwater above solid ice
questions.explanation: Estuaries and mangrove swamps often hold brackish water.

questions.prompt: What forms where a river deposits sediment near its mouth?
questions.explanation: The Nile and Mississippi deltas are well-known examples. The name comes from the triangular Greek letter Δ.

questions.prompt: What is a tributary?
choices: A channel splitting away from a river
A stream flowing into another stream
A lake with no permanent outlet
A spring flowing from an aquifer
questions.explanation: The Missouri River, for example, is a tributary of the Mississippi.

questions.prompt: What is a watershed?
choices: Land draining to a common outlet
A channel dug to connect two lakes
questions.explanation: A watershed, also called a drainage basin, can be as small as a creek's or as large as the Mississippi's.

questions.prompt: Which lake is the deepest in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia is about 1,640 m deep and holds roughly a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water.

questions.prompt: Which of the five Great Lakes has the largest surface area?
questions.explanation: Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest inland body of water by surface area?
questions.explanation: Despite its name, the Caspian Sea is an enclosed inland body of water.

questions.prompt: Which strait connects the Mediterranean Sea to the Atlantic Ocean?
questions.explanation: At its narrowest the strait is only about 13 km (8 miles) wide.

questions.prompt: Which two seas are linked by the Suez Canal?
questions.explanation: The canal opened in 1869 and lets ships avoid sailing around Africa.

questions.prompt: Reef-building corals are plants.
questions.explanation: Corals are animals. Many live with photosynthetic algae in their tissues.

questions.prompt: The five North American Great Lakes contain freshwater.
questions.explanation: They form a connected freshwater system that drains toward the Atlantic.

questions.prompt: What is upwelling?
questions.answer: The rise of deeper water toward the surface, often bringing nutrients into sunlit water.
questions.explanation: Upwelling off Peru and California supports some of the world's most productive fisheries.

questions.prompt: What is the water cycle?
questions.answer: The ongoing movement of water through processes such as evaporation, condensation, precipitation and runoff.
questions.explanation: The Sun's energy drives evaporation, and gravity brings water back down as precipitation and runoff.
